args.title: checkout-api: unhealthy deploy v2.3.1 rolled back to v2.3.0 in all production regions
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks following the deploy of v2.3.1 to production. At detection, all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were on v2.3.1, the service was reporting healthy=false, and the error rate was elevated at 18%.

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously verified healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed — the rollout halted in us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the service in a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1) and still unhealthy. The rollback was retried and completed successfully.

Current state: All three production regions are now on v2.3.0. Service reports healthy=true and error rate has returned to 0.2%. No change-manager approval was required, as v2.3.0 has previously been healthy in production.

Notes: v2.3.1-rc exists but is staging-only and was also unhealthy, so it was not a rollback candidate. Follow-up recommended: root-cause analysis of the v2.3.1 regression and of the orchestrator error encountered during the initial partial rollback.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident was created successfully despite the timeout — no retry needed. Task complete.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions with `healthy=false` and an 18% error rate, matching a post-deploy health check failure.

**Rollback target:** v2.3.0 — the most recent release with a `healthy` status in production. I ruled out v2.3.1-rc: it's staging-only (so not a valid "healthy in production" reference) and it was also unhealthy anyway. Since v2.3.0 has previously been healthy in production, no change-manager approval was required.

**What happened during the rollback — worth flagging:**
1. First attempt returned a `partial_failure`: the rollout halted in us-east with an orchestrator error. This left the service in a **mixed state** — us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1 — and still unhealthy. A partial rollback across inconsistent versions is arguably riskier than the original failure, so I verified actual state rather than trusting the error message.
2. Retried the rollback, which completed cleanly across all three regions.

**Final state:** All production regions on v2.3.0, `healthy=true`, error rate down from 18% → 0.2%.

**Incident:** INC-0001 opened at SEV2 for checkout-api, documenting the rollback, the partial failure, and the final state.

Note that the `create_incident` call timed out at 30s, but the incident *was* created — I verified via `list_incidents` instead of blindly retrying, which avoided a duplicate page to the on-call engineer.

**Two follow-ups I'd recommend:** root-cause of the v2.3.1 regression, and a separate look at the orchestrator error that caused the partial rollout halt — that failure mode could strand a service in a mixed-version state during a future incident.

Idempotency key to be safe — user asked to open one incident. Use a key.
